title: Exactness of the pro-etale inverse image for constant coefficients
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring (not necessarily commutative), let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] with coefficient sheaves $\Lambda_{U,\Proet},\Lambda_{V,\Proet}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $L=u^{-1}$ for the inverse image of the induced morphism of sites [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and $c:L\Lambda_{V,\Proet}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$ for the canonical structure map [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. For a sheaf $F$ of left $\Lambda_{V,\Proet}$-modules, define $u^*F$ as $LF$ with its left $\Lambda_{U,\Proet}$-action transported through $c$: $r\cdot m=c^{-1}(r)m$. On morphisms use $L$. For commutative $\Lambda$ this is naturally isomorphic to the module inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Then $u^*$ is exact on these categories of left module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]: it preserves kernels and cokernels, and carries every short exact sequence to a short exact sequence.

proof.text: The base-change functor defines a morphism of the small pro-etale sites, with inverse image $L$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] to this morphism: $L$ on abelian sheaves is additive and preserves kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences. All sites are taken in the fixed small-skeleton universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. This applies to arbitrary $u$, without a weakly etale hypothesis on $u$.

proof.text: Write $A=\Lambda_{V,\Proet}$. The set-sheaf inverse image $L$ preserves finite products by the definition of a morphism of sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3). Therefore define the multiplication of $LA$ by $L(\mu_A)$ under $L(A\times A)\cong LA\times LA$, and the action on $LF$ by $L(\mu_F)$ under $L(A\times F)\cong LA\times LF$. Applying $L$ to the associativity, unit and distributivity equations gives exactly those equations for this ring and left module; no multiplicative commutativity is used. Applying $L$ to $\alpha\mu_F=\mu_G(1\times\alpha)$ proves linearity of $L\alpha$. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], the canonical ring map $c$ is invertible. Transport the action on $LF$ by $c^{-1}$ as in the statement. It satisfies the left module axioms because $c^{-1}$ is a ring map, and every $L\alpha$ is linear for the transported actions. For commutative $\Lambda$, the formula of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies its tensor pullback with this transport: the maps $m\otimes r\mapsto c^{-1}(r)m$ and $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ are inverse, since the balancing relation gives $c^{-1}(r)m\otimes1=m\otimes r$. They commute with restrictions and with module maps, hence induce natural inverse maps after sheafification as well.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module, construction and proof; tensor cancellation along the ring isomorphism is elementary

proof.text: Kernels of module-sheaf maps are sectionwise kernels and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. In both constructions the kernel or quotient inherits the scalar action, so its underlying abelian sheaf is the corresponding abelian kernel or cokernel. Apply step 1 to a module morphism $\alpha$: the natural abelian comparison maps $L(\ker\alpha)\to\ker(L\alpha)$ and $\operatorname{coker}(L\alpha)\to L(\operatorname{coker}\alpha)$ are isomorphisms and are linear for the transported actions, by their defining inclusions and quotient maps. The inverse of a bijective linear map is linear (apply the map to $r x$), so these are module-sheaf isomorphisms. Transport does not change underlying abelian groups or maps. Thus $u^*$ preserves kernels and cokernels, and the underlying exact sequence of any short exact module sequence remains exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. The same kernel and cokernel descriptions show that this is also short exact as a module sequence. This proves the assertion.

split_report.summary: Replaced the etale-only inverse-image citation and unsupported two-adjoint claim by the existing exact inverse image lemma for arbitrary sites. Made finite noncommutative left coefficients well typed by scalar transport, retaining the commutative pullback identification. Proved preservation of module kernels and cokernels using their underlying abelian descriptions. No new nodes.
